briefFidelity: FAIL. The brief asks for a container form -- concentric enclosure, one boundary inside another, with a small dense centre held at the middle. Blind, I described the opposite grammar: a dominant central body ringed by a single regular array of smaller satellites, i.e. a radial burst, and I reached for the words 'starburst' and 'snowflake' for 9190 and 'messy cluster' for 9727 without any prompting. Nothing I saw was nested; there is no second boundary inside a first anywhere in the twelve. 9548 is the closest to an enclosure and it holds nothing at all -- an empty centre, which is the one thing the brief specified must be filled. The brief also asks for sparing gold over deep ink with most of the frame given to the dark; 9369, 9906 and 10085 are dominated by a solid gold disc covering most of the frame, which inverts that ratio outright. And the brief says what varies between tokens is the number of enclosures and the character of the centre -- what I actually recorded varying was primitive family (triangle / square / circle), symmetry order, brightness and density. The stated variation axis is not the delivered one.
seedVariation: Twelve distinguishable works, not one work twelve times -- but varied along the wrong axis. At 120px the bright half (9369, 9906, 10085, 10443, 9190, 9727) separates cleanly by silhouette family. The weak end is 10264 / 10622 / 10801, which I flagged blind as reading like three variations of the same dim triangle cluster. So neither extreme failure applies; this is not the reason for the refusal.
thumbnailSurvival: Partial. Silhouette and gross density survive for roughly eight of twelve. The dark-ramp tokens do not: 10622, 10801 and 10980 drop to low-contrast brown smudges on near-black, with 10801 barely separating from the ground. Internal structure is lost everywhere -- 9369's layered rosette and its 'eye' flatten to a dark blob at browse size.
marketResponse: Visible, and that is the failure. The brief asks for a change 'nothing that a casual viewer would notice at thumbnail size' and explicitly says do not manufacture drama. Blind at 256px I recorded 9369's dominant gold disc vanishing entirely under stress, 9548's eight-square ring collapsing to three scattered squares, 9190 contracting to roughly 60% scale, and recovery introducing bright stroke-only outline geometry that did not exist in neutral (9011's large outlined triangle, 9548's gold zigzag ring). A frame-filling gold disc becoming a small dark knot is unmissable at 120px, let alone subtle. The change is not the claimed change: 'slight tightening or loosening of the enclosure' is a modulation, and what ships is appearance, disappearance and rescaling of primary elements.
tokenIdentity: Holds, and this is the strongest axis. 9369 stays the disc-with-eye, 9190 the six-point star, 9548 the square ring, 9011 the triangle trio across all three conditions. The one strain is 9369 under stress, where the token loses the single feature that identifies it.
composition: Centred, generous margin, clean focal hierarchy on the disc-anchored tokens. Defects: 10980 clips shapes at the top-left and bottom-right corners; 9727 is cluttered rather than composed; the three dark tokens mush at browse size. No rendering artifacts otherwise -- the transparency stacking is clean and the single-hue discipline is genuinely well held.
reasoning: My stage-1 description, written with no knowledge of the brief, is a description of a radial satellite burst with a dramatic market response -- and the brief asks for a concentric container with a market response a casual viewer would not notice. Those are not near-misses in wording; they are the two load-bearing clauses of the brief, and my blind reading contradicts both. I described satellites orbiting a core where nested boundaries were required, I described an empty centre in the one token that does enclose, I described a frame-filling gold disc where the brief reserved most of the frame for the dark, and I described the dominant element of a token disappearing outright where the brief asked for a faint tightening and warned against manufactured drama. The craft is real -- the hue discipline, the transparency stacking, the centring and the token identity across conditions are all competent, and the seeds are genuinely twelve things. But this is a permanent on-chain commitment, and the gate is fidelity: this reads as an energetic radial emblem that responds loudly to the market, not as a still contemplative reliquary that barely acknowledges it.
wouldChange: Rebuild the form as actual concentric enclosure -- two or more nested boundaries with a small dense centre held inside them, the number of rings being the per-token variable -- and let the market act only on ring spacing or stroke weight. That one change fixes both failures at once: the drama is currently possible because the market is allowed to add, remove and rescale primary elements, and a nested-ring form has a natural quiet modulation (tighten or loosen the gaps) that cannot manufacture drama even if the sensor swings hard.
